spans.text: ...Late at night, in the Commander's office at the Griffin base.
There is a long line of Dolls standing outside the door as the heads of each department wait for their duty assignments.
Thanks to the supplies provided by Havier, roughly 50% of the Dolls in the Griffin base have been rebuilt, enough to sustain basic operations for the base.
However, my inbox is still full of pending work requests...
Commander, this is a list of the discrepancies between the manifest and our actual inventory. I've sent a copy to your inbox and filed a copy in the system.
Alright, I'll look at it right away.
Are you sure you don't need a break? You don't look well...
It's okay, I'm fine.
Springfield looks like she wants to say something else, but in the end she decides against it and simply leaves the office.
The canteen has submitted its ingredients purchase list and budget for approval, Commander. Please take a look at it.
Alright, I will.
A pile of documents suddenly collapses and Gr G36 stacks them back up again before leaving the office without a word.
Commander, I.O.P. is asking for confirmation of receipt for the most recent batch of supplies.
Hang on, where did Springfield's list go...
I dive into the pile of documents and rummage through them...
Kalina, help me ask Springfield about her comparison list.
The only sound in the silent office is my rummaging through files and folders.
Is there a flash sale on?
Don't get distracted, Kalina!
The person who ought to have appeared by my side with a smile on her face still hasn't shown up yet.
...Kalina?
I look back and realize that there is nobody behind me.
The only things in this massive office are work documents and my dejected self.
...How could I have forgotten, Kalina's on leave.
I reach past the documents on my desk for my coffee mug, planning to gulp it all down. However, the mug is empty save for two or three-day-old coffee stains.
...Several days ago, during a regular checkup for the human personnel at the Griffin base.
Commander, we're the only ones who haven't gone for our checkup yet!
Right, another routine physical...
Let me take care of the work I have on hand first.
Commander, don't keep burying yourself in work! Your health is important too, you know!
(Coughs)
I'm fine, but you haven't been feeling too well yourself, have you?
It seems like you've been coughing for a long time now. Are you showing symptoms from your time in the sub base?
I'm fine, it's just a small cold.
Anyway, don't change the subject! Go for your checkup already!
But there's still so much work to do...
I'm here, aren't I? I'll help share your burden!
Now go, it won't take long!
At Kalina's urging, I reluctantly go for my checkup.
Two hours later, the checkup is complete.
It turned out well. I told you, I didn't need it. I could have approved so many documents during that...
Kalina's checkup ended long ago, and now she's curled up on a tiny chair in the waiting area. She seems to be asleep.
Kalina?
Are you asleep?
As I see her tremble slightly in her slumber, I take off my coat and drape it over her body.
I can't believe you could actually fall asleep in a tiny place like this...
You must be exhausted from all the work in last few days.
Kalina remains soundly asleep and does not respond.
I sigh and gently run my fingers through her hair, but I feel a burning heat rise up through my fingertips.
...A fever? You need to see a doctor.
No...no shots...
Must...work...
This is no time to be stubborn.
I ignore Kalina's drowsy mumbling and gently scoop her up in my arms before hurrying over to the doctor's office...
I open Kalina's medical report again. I don't know how many times I've done this already.
The harm to her body inflicted by her sustained high fever has been converted to numerical data, which are seared in my mind.
Self-reproach. Guilt. Regret.
A complex mass of emotions writhes within my heart, gnawing at my soul like a swarm of ants.
She's going to get better...
The doctor said that Kalina can be discharged soon, provided her condition doesn't worsen.
A petty little sickness like this won't beat someone as tough as her.
Knock knock knock—
Someone is politely knocking on my desk from behind me.
...I thought you had passed out, Commander. Why didn't you take my call?
I didn't notice...
I hurriedly shove the medical report into the depths of my drawer.
What is it, did some urgent work come up?
Firstly, I'm here to remind you to send the supply receipt confirmation I mentioned earlier.
Second...
The schedule for the Sangvis training ground has been cleared out.
Huh? The Sangvis training ground? Why?
Judging from Kalina's work diary, the Sangvis training ground is being temporarily used as a Paradeus special drill area due to a lack of suitable venues.
The Paradeus special drill...
Right, I understand.
Mm. I'll be going, then.
Thank you.
Please take care of yourself, Commander.
Helian looks at my face with a worried expression of her own. She sighs and leaves.
I look through Kalina's desk and find the Paradeus special drill program that she has compiled earlier.
The early phases of the program are almost complete. After that, all that remains is to carry out several rounds of statistical analysis.
Kalin, once you get back, I'm going to show you that everything is still running smoothly, the way you left it.
I tighten my grip on the program sheet in my hand. Kalina smiles at me from the picture on the desk.
